types.title: Record economic events in ledger accounts, gross profit and merchandise balance

economic_events: The company sold inventory worth 240 thousand USD to its domestic partner for 550 thousand USD in cash.
Our company purchased inventory worth 310 thousand USD. Payment for the inventory is due in 30 days.
Our company complained about the quality of the goods upon receipt, so it subsequently requested and received a 20% discount. The invoice was corrected.
Our company has transferred its entire trade payables from the settlement deposit account. The settlement deposit account debit notification has been received.
tasks.task: Record economic events in thousands of USD! Answer the questions! Only write the amount on the appropriate side of the ledger accounts, NOT the event number!

questions.prompt: What is the Gross Profit from Sales?
questions.format: for a profit: +1234, for a loss: -1234

questions.prompt: What is the merchandise account balance at the end of the period?
questions.format: only the amount, without spaces or other punctuation marks

tasks.explanation: Gross profit = sales revenue 550 - cost of goods sold 240 = 310. Goods: 800 - 240 + 310 - 62 = 808. The discount is 20% of 310 = 62; the remaining payable 310 - 62 = 248 is paid from the bank account.

tasks.prompt:
At Birchwood Supplies, you know the following information about the period in question:
• Beginning balance of Accounts receivable is 2,200 Th USD,
• 400 Th USD was received into the bank account for a previous sale,
• Inventory worth 3,900 Th USD was invoiced for 5,500 Th USD, with a payment deadline of 10 days,
• A customer paid in cash for a previous sale of 300 Th USD.
How much is the credit turnover of Accounts receivable on the period-end general ledger statement?
tasks.explanation: The credit side shows the decreases: 400 + 300 = 700 Th USD. The sale (5,500) is a debit; the closing balance is 7,000.

types.title: Operating profit of a manufacturer (financial items left out)

tasks.prompt: A manufacturing company achieved 350 thUSD in revenue during the year. Its material-type expenses were 30 thUSD, personnel-type expenses 50 thUSD, and depreciation 30 thUSD. The company paid 110 thUSD in interest, and had 60 thUSD in other expenses and 130 thUSD in other income. Determine the operating profit!
tasks.explanation: Operating profit = 350 - 30 - 50 - 30 - 60 + 130 = 310 thUSD. The interest paid is a financial item, so it is not part of the operating profit.

tasks.prompt: A manufacturing company achieved 580 thUSD in revenue during the year. Its material-type expenses were 100 thUSD, personnel-type expenses 50 thUSD, and depreciation 20 thUSD. The company paid 110 thUSD in interest, and had 70 thUSD in other expenses and 70 thUSD in other income. Determine the operating profit!
tasks.explanation: Operating profit = 580 - 100 - 50 - 20 - 70 + 70 = 410 thUSD. The interest paid is a financial item, so it is not part of the operating profit.

tasks.prompt: A manufacturing company achieved 610 thUSD in revenue during the year. Its material-type expenses were 130 thUSD, personnel-type expenses 40 thUSD, and depreciation 50 thUSD. The company paid 80 thUSD in interest, and had 60 thUSD in other expenses and 110 thUSD in other income. Determine the operating profit!
tasks.explanation: Operating profit = 610 - 130 - 40 - 50 - 60 + 110 = 440 thUSD. The interest paid is a financial item, so it is not part of the operating profit.

tasks.prompt: A manufacturing company achieved 610 thUSD in revenue during the year. Its material-type expenses were 130 thUSD, personnel-type expenses 50 thUSD, and depreciation 30 thUSD. The company received 120 thUSD in interest, and had 60 thUSD in other expenses and 70 thUSD in other income. Determine the operating profit!
tasks.explanation: Operating profit = 610 - 130 - 50 - 30 - 60 + 70 = 410 thUSD. The interest received is a financial item, so it is not part of the operating profit.

tasks.prompt: A manufacturing company achieved 630 thUSD in revenue during the year. Its material-type expenses were 120 thUSD, personnel-type expenses 100 thUSD, and depreciation 10 thUSD. The company received 30 thUSD in interest, and had 20 thUSD in other expenses and 60 thUSD in other income. Determine the operating profit!
tasks.explanation: Operating profit = 630 - 120 - 100 - 10 - 20 + 60 = 440 thUSD. The interest received is a financial item, so it is not part of the operating profit.

types.title: Gross profit of a sale with an advance

tasks.prompt: A business has a sales price of 450 USD, for this transaction the buyer previously gave an advance of 200 USD, and the purchase price of the goods was 250 USD. What is the business's gross profit?
tasks.explanation: Gross profit = sales price - purchase price = 450 - 250 = 200 USD. The advance of 200 USD only decides when the money arrived.

tasks.prompt: A business has a sales price of 550 USD, for this transaction the buyer previously gave an advance of 250 USD, and the purchase price of the goods was 150 USD. What is the business's gross profit?
tasks.explanation: Gross profit = sales price - purchase price = 550 - 150 = 400 USD. The advance of 250 USD only decides when the money arrived.

tasks.prompt: A business has a sales price of 500 USD, for this transaction the buyer previously gave an advance of 100 USD, and the purchase price of the goods was 200 USD. What is the business's gross profit?
tasks.explanation: Gross profit = sales price - purchase price = 500 - 200 = 300 USD. The advance of 100 USD only decides when the money arrived.

tasks.prompt: A business has a sales price of 1050 USD, for this transaction the buyer previously gave an advance of 250 USD, and the purchase price of the goods was 900 USD. What is the business's gross profit?
tasks.explanation: Gross profit = sales price - purchase price = 1050 - 900 = 150 USD. The advance of 250 USD only decides when the money arrived.

tasks.prompt: A business has a sales price of 900 USD, for this transaction the buyer previously gave an advance of 350 USD, and the purchase price of the goods was 300 USD. What is the business's gross profit?
tasks.explanation: Gross profit = sales price - purchase price = 900 - 300 = 600 USD. The advance of 350 USD only decides when the money arrived.

types.title: Debit and credit of a transaction

tasks.prompt: Paying a supplier's invoice from the bank account would result in which of the following?
options: A debit to both trade payables and bank account.
A debit to bank account and a credit to trade payables.
A debit to trade payables and a credit to bank account.
A debit to trade payables and a credit to goods.
tasks.explanation: The liability decreases (debit) and the bank balance decreases (credit).

tasks.prompt: Purchasing goods on credit would result in which of the following?
options: A debit to goods and a credit to trade payables.
A debit to goods and a credit to cash.
A debit to trade payables and a credit to goods.
A credit to both goods and trade payables.
tasks.explanation: The inventory increases (debit) and the liability increases (credit).

tasks.prompt: The owners investing cash in the company would result in which of the following?
options: A debit to contributed capital and a credit to cash.
A debit to cash and a credit to bank loan.
A debit to cash and a credit to contributed capital.
A debit to both cash and contributed capital.
tasks.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and the owners' capital increases (credit).

tasks.prompt: Repaying a bank loan from cash would result in which of the following?
options: A debit to cash and a credit to bank loan.
A credit to both bank loan and cash.
A debit to bank loan and a credit to cash.
A debit to bank loan and a credit to contributed capital.
tasks.explanation: The liability decreases (debit) and cash decreases (credit).

tasks.prompt: A chronological record of all transactions of a company is called a(n):
tasks.explanation: The journal records the transactions in the order in which they happen.

tasks.prompt: A list of all account balances at a point in time, used to check that total debits equal total credits, is called a(n):
tasks.explanation: The trial balance lists the balances of all accounts.

tasks.prompt: The collection of all the accounts of a company is called the:
tasks.explanation: The ledger contains all the accounts.

tasks.prompt: The process of transferring the amounts from the journal to the accounts is called:
tasks.explanation: Posting moves the journal entries into the ledger accounts.

tasks.prompt: The adjusted trial balance is prepared after:
options: the adjusting entries have been posted to the ledger.
the post-closing trial balance is prepared.
tasks.explanation: Adjusting entries come first; the financial statements are then prepared from the adjusted trial balance.

tasks.prompt: Adjusting entries are made:
options: at the end of the accounting period before the financial statements are prepared.
only at the beginning of the period.
after the financial statements are issued.
tasks.explanation: They bring the accounts up to date before the statements are prepared.

tasks.prompt: Which financial statement is prepared first?
tasks.explanation: The profit from the income statement is needed for the equity and then for the balance sheet.

tasks.prompt: The trial balance is used to check that:
tasks.explanation: A balanced trial balance only proves that debits equal credits.

tasks.prompt: Liabilities do not include:
tasks.explanation: Accounts receivable are assets.

tasks.prompt: Stockholders' equity does not include:
options: Profit after tax for the year
tasks.explanation: A bank loan is a liability.

tasks.prompt: Current assets do not include:
tasks.explanation: Machinery is a non-current (fixed) tangible asset.

tasks.prompt: Non-current assets do not include:
tasks.explanation: Raw materials are inventories, which are current assets.

tasks.prompt: The operating profit is increased by:
tasks.explanation: The gain on the sale of equipment is other income; the other items are financial income.

tasks.prompt: The profit from financial transactions is decreased by:
tasks.explanation: Interest paid on loans is a financial expense; the other items are operating expenses.

tasks.prompt: The operating profit is decreased by:
tasks.explanation: Depreciation is an operating expense; the other items belong to the financial transactions.

tasks.prompt: The profit from financial transactions is increased by:
options: Interest received on long-term loans granted
tasks.explanation: Interest received is financial income; the other items belong to the operating profit.

tasks.prompt: Which of the following slows down the collection of receivables?
tasks.explanation: A longer payment deadline means the customers pay later.

tasks.prompt: Which of the following measures reduces the risk of bad debts?
options: Issuing invoices as late as possible
Selling to all customers on credit without limits
Checking the creditworthiness of customers before selling on credit
tasks.explanation: Checking the customers keeps unreliable payers away.

tasks.prompt: Why does a company grant a cash discount to its customers?
options: To encourage customers to pay earlier
tasks.explanation: The discount is the reward for early payment.

tasks.prompt: Which action speeds up the cash inflow from customers?
tasks.explanation: An advance brings the money in before the delivery.

tasks.prompt: What does a cash budget show?
options: Planned cash inflows and outflows for a future period
The profit of the previous year
The amount of tax payable to the authorities
tasks.explanation: A cash budget plans the cash movements.

tasks.prompt: Which of the following is a cash inflow in a cash budget?
tasks.explanation: Money received from customers is an inflow.

tasks.prompt: Which of the following is NOT included in a cash budget?
tasks.explanation: Depreciation is not a cash movement.

tasks.prompt: Who mainly uses a cash budget?
options: Auditors, to certify the balance sheet
The tax authority, to assess VAT
tasks.explanation: The cash budget is an internal planning tool.
